title: How to provide secrets to a workshop

steps.text: Build the workshop snap from canonical/workshop secrets-implementation at ae7134e8 with snapcraft pack in a scratch checkout
Launch a throwaway Ubuntu 24.04 LXD VM, initialize LXD inside it, install the built snap, and start a headless GNOME Keyring for the ubuntu user
Store a throwaway credential in the host keyring with secret-tool store using identifying attributes, and confirm the lookup finds it
Write a workshop definition with a system SDK secret slot that carries lookup attributes only, plus the uv SDK with a stand-in secret plug
Launch the workshop and confirm in workshop connections that the secret plug is not connected
Connect the plug to the slot with workshop connect and confirm the manual connection in workshop connections
Inside the workshop, read the secret with workshopctl get-secret as an SDK wrapper would, and confirm the throwaway value arrives
Refresh the workshop and confirm the connection persists
Lock the keyring and capture what retrieval reports
Point the slot at attributes that match no keyring item and capture the error
Store a second keyring item with the same attributes and capture the error
Disconnect the plug and confirm retrieval is refused
Run workshop exec with --env NAME while NAME is set in the calling shell, then with NAME unset, and confirm the unset name is skipped without an error
Run workshop exec with --env NAME=value, then run workshop exec again without the flag and confirm the value is gone
